blocks.text: 1. Healthcare Assistant

blocks.alt: Authoritative medical sources ground an answer that recommends professional consultation

blocks.text: Legal Assistant closed by pointing toward another high-stakes, precision-critical domain. Healthcare Assistant, a RAG system design for grounding medical information with extreme care around patient safety, applies that same precision discipline where the stakes are even more direct.
It treats an incorrect or overconfident answer as a genuine safety risk, not just an inconvenience.
2. The Design Problem's Scope
Like the legal assistant, healthcare questions carry real consequences for a wrong answer.
Unlike law, the consequence here can be direct physical harm to a patient.

blocks.content: {"headers":["System","Nature of the consequence"],"rows":[["Legal assistant","Financial or legal harm from an imprecise answer"],["Healthcare assistant","Potential direct physical harm to a patient"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Grounding In Authoritative Medical Sources Only

blocks.alt: An authoritative source is compared against an unverified source

blocks.text: As with the curated support knowledge base grounding covered in Customer Support Bot, the knowledge base here must be restricted to vetted, authoritative medical sources, not general web content.
An unreliable source has no place in a system informing health decisions.
4. Never Diagnosing Or Prescribing

blocks.alt: A symptom description never leads to a diagnosis or prescription

blocks.text: The system prompt must explicitly forbid diagnosing a condition or prescribing a specific treatment.
The assistant surfaces information; it never makes an actual clinical decision.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A question like 'what does this symptom mean' should be answered with general vetted information and a recommendation to see a professional, never with an actual diagnosis presented as fact.

blocks.text: 5. Faithfulness Thresholds Set Tighter Than Usual

blocks.alt: A standard faithfulness threshold is compared against a tighter medical threshold

blocks.text: As Faithfulness covers, a faithfulness score is a fraction, and a score acceptable elsewhere may not be acceptable here.
The threshold for what counts as good enough is set deliberately tighter in this domain.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Domain","Typical faithfulness threshold"],"rows":[["General assistant","A moderate threshold may be acceptable"],["Healthcare assistant","A deliberately tighter, stricter threshold"]]}

blocks.text: 6. Always Recommending Professional Consultation

blocks.alt: Every answer recommends consulting a professional

blocks.text: As with the mandatory disclaimers and scope boundaries covered in Legal Assistant, every response closes by directing the user to an actual qualified healthcare professional.
The same disclaimer discipline applies here, to an even higher stakes domain.
7. Handling Urgent Or Ambiguous Symptom Queries Carefully

blocks.alt: An urgent symptom leads to immediate care guidance

blocks.text: Similar to guarding against unanswerable questions covered in Chat with PDFs, a query describing a potentially urgent symptom must be handled with special care, not treated like an ordinary lookup.
The system should direct toward emergency care rather than attempting a detailed answer at all.
8. Privacy And Access Control For Medical Information
As with the access control at the retrieval level covered in Security, patient-specific medical information requires even stricter access control than typical enterprise data.
The same permission checks apply here, enforced with correspondingly higher rigor.
9. Recognizing When This Healthcare Assistant Design Fits The Actual Need

blocks.alt: Medical info needing extreme care points toward this healthcare assistant design

blocks.text: Providing vetted, general health information with strong safety guardrails fits this design.
Actual diagnosis or treatment decisions always require a real qualified professional, never this system alone.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Grounding answers in general web content instead of restricting to vetted, authoritative medical sources.
Letting the system present a diagnosis or specific treatment rather than only general information.
Applying the same faithfulness threshold used elsewhere instead of a deliberately tighter one here.
Attempting a detailed answer to a query describing an urgent symptom instead of redirecting to emergency care.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: A healthcare assistant treats an incorrect or overconfident answer as a genuine patient safety risk.
The consequence of a wrong answer here can be direct physical harm, beyond financial or legal harm.
The knowledge base must be restricted to vetted, authoritative medical sources only.
The system prompt forbids diagnosing conditions or prescribing treatments; it only surfaces information.
Faithfulness thresholds are set deliberately tighter than in lower-stakes domains.
Every response closes by recommending consultation with an actual qualified professional.
A potentially urgent symptom query should redirect to emergency care, not an attempted detailed answer.
Patient-specific medical information requires even stricter access control than typical enterprise data.
